function_question: How does nature build efficient networks?

opening.text: There was a girl called Zara, 14, who cycled everywhere and joined every town planning workshop she could.
Zara rode past schools that were only a few minutes apart, yet had no safe path between them.
The town announced new bike paths to link its 6 schools. "Every metre costs money," said the planner, "but one closed path must never cut a school off." Zara grabbed a pencil.

card.problem: 6 schools need linking with little path
card.goal: A short network that survives a break

guide.brief: I'm Popi, your story guide. Zara's town must link 6 schools with bike paths, using as little path as possible, and one closure must never cut a school off. Can you help her? Let's start!
guide.your_idea: Some planners already have a network in mind. Do you?
guide.nature_clues: A brainless blob once copied Tokyo's railways! Tap each card to meet four network experts.
guide.design_secret: Here's the strategy all four heroes share…
guide.skill: Engineers measure before they argue. Which network will be shortest: star, chain or ring? Predict first, then measure the string.
guide.sketch: Draw your network like a slime mold would: thick main routes, thin backup loops.
guide.build_and_test: Measure your network's total length, then snip the links one at a time. How many breaks can it survive?
guide.retry_tip: Add one 120° junction or move one loop, then measure again. Did you save length without losing safety?
guide.ending: And ever since then, kids in Zara's town cycle between all 6 schools, and a closed path never leaves anyone stranded!

quick_check.question: Zara's shortest network is 60 cm long. Adding one backup loop adds 12 cm. How much longer is the network, as a percentage?
quick_check.right: Right! 12 ÷ 60 = 0.2, which is 20%. That's the price of a network that survives a break.
quick_check.wrong: Not quite. Divide the extra length by the original length: 12 ÷ 60.

clue_cards.name: Slime mold
clue_cards.trick: It grows tubes everywhere, then keeps only the busiest ones.
clue_cards.does: In about a day, it grew a network as efficient as Tokyo's real railway.

clue_cards.name: Leaf veins
clue_cards.trick: Its smallest veins join up into loops.
clue_cards.does: If a vein is bitten through, water flows the other way round the loop.

clue_cards.name: Ant trails
clue_cards.trick: Scent trails on shorter paths get topped up faster.
clue_cards.does: More ants follow the stronger scent, so the colony picks the shortest route.

clue_cards.name: Fungal mycelium
clue_cards.trick: Thin fungal threads join tree roots under the soil.
clue_cards.does: Busy threads grow thicker, and unused ones fade away.

predict.prompt: Can one break cut it, or does it have a backup? Predict first!

items.label: One path snaking through all 6 schools
A ring road around all 6 schools

predict.explain: A network with no loops is cheap, but every link is a weak spot. A loop gives each place two ways in, so one break can't cut anyone off. That safety costs extra length.

lab.title: The network string lab
lab.predict: Link 6 pins with string in four different ways. Which network uses the least string?

tool.name: Nature Translator
tool.intro: The Nature Translator turns a design problem into a question for nature, then turns nature's answer back into a design. It has 4 steps, and today you'll use all of them.

parts.name: Function
parts.what: What must my design DO? Start with a verb.
parts.example: 🧥 Keep a person dry while letting sweat escape.
parts.starter: My network must connect 6 schools while…

parts.name: Nature question
parts.example: 🧥 How does nature stay dry but still breathe?
parts.starter: How does nature connect many places with…?

parts.name: Strategy
parts.what: Which living thing does it, and how?
parts.example: 🧥 A duck's feathers overlap like roof tiles and are coated in oil, so rain runs off but air still moves between them.
parts.starter: The slime mold does it by…

parts.name: Design principle
parts.what: Say the trick in plain words, without the living thing.
parts.example: 🧥 Overlapping, water-repelling layers shed rain but leave gaps for air.
parts.starter: Without the slime mold, the trick is: grow many paths, then…

sketch_checklist: I drew all 6 schools and every link between them.
I showed main routes thick and backup loops thin.
I wrote my predicted total length in cm.

test.measure: total path length in cm (and how many paths can break before a school is cut off)
test.check_question: Robustness check: how many single links can break without cutting a school off?

reflection.question: Which nature trick shaped your network the most?
